description: WHEN DFHRESP(NOTFND) of 9400-GETCUSTDATA-BYCUST at :839-857, the SECOND arm of the three-arm EVALUATE WS-RESP-CD at :836, whose WHEN order - NORMAL at :837, NOTFND at :839, OTHER at :858 - is preserved exactly (gate G30). The folder pins nine read outcomes across three call sites with no two cases overlapping (gate G47): case03 drives all three reads to NORMAL, case08 the 9200 NOTFND at :741 and case09 the 9200 WHEN OTHER at :759 on the CXACAIX path, case10 the 9300 NOTFND at :789 and case11 the 9300 WHEN OTHER at :809 on ACCTDAT, case13 the 9400 WHEN OTHER at :858 - and this file is the only one that pins the 9400 NOTFND arm, so removing or re-pointing it would leave that arm undriven. Nothing is forced here: forcedOutcomes is empty because the miss comes from the seeded rows, which is the stronger form of the assertion. CCXREF holds fixture rows 0-2, whose XREF-ACCT-ID spans are accounts 50, 27 and 2 and whose first row carries XREF-CUST-ID 000000050 and XREF-CARD-NUM 0500024453765740; ACCTDAT holds fixture row 49, which is account 00000000050; CUSTDAT holds fixture row 0, which is customer 000000001. So the cross-reference READ at :727 succeeds and :739-740 move the customer id and the card number into the commarea, the account READ at :776 succeeds and :788 sets FOUND-ACCT-IN-MASTER, and the customer READ at :826 - keyed by WS-CARD-RID-CUST-ID-X, the PIC X(09) REDEFINES at :76-77 of the id the cross reference supplied - looks for 000000050 in a file holding only 000000001 and reports NOTFND. The cross-reference site is the CXACAIX PATH over the CCXREF base, reached through the one CardXrefRepository alternate-key finder and never through a second repository or a second table (gate G45). Two details separate this arm from the three WHEN OTHER arms. It sets FLG-CUSTFILTER-NOT-OK at :841 - the CUSTOMER flag, not the account flag the other two failure paragraphs set - so 1300 leaves ACCTSIDC at the DFHDFCOL it moved at :555: the IF FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK at :557-559 does not fire, and neither does the blank-and-REENTER pair at :561-565 that would add the asterisk, so a customer failure never colours the account number red (gate G38, the negative half of the pair case05 makes positive), and the two identical-bodied arms of the cursor EVALUATE at :546-552 are preserved rather than collapsed. And it moves ERROR-RESP and ERROR-RESP2 at :843-844 OUTSIDE the IF WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF guard at :845, where 9200 moves them inside it at :745-746, so those two fields are updated even on a run whose message is not. The SET DID-NOT-FIND-CUST-IN-CUSTDAT that would have marked the miss is commented out at :842, which leaves the guard at :713-715 permanently false - immaterial only because 9400 is the last read - and it stays commented, as do the PERFORM SEND-LONG-TEXT at :866-867 and the direct MOVE CUST-SSN at :495 that the hyphenating STRING at :496-504 replaced (practice B5). The cross-width truncation is what this case exists to pin, and it is the dangerous kind. The STRING at :846-856 concatenates 'CustId:' (7) + WS-CARD-RID-CUST-ID-X (9) + ' not found' (10) + ' in customer master.Resp: ' (26, with a full stop and a trailing space) + ERROR-RESP (10) + ' REAS:' (6) + ERROR-RESP2 (10) = 7+9+10+26+10+6+10 = 78 characters INTO WS-RETURN-MSG PIC X(75) at :117. A COBOL alphanumeric receiver truncates on the RIGHT, so the last 3 bytes are discarded - and here they are the tail of ERROR-RESP2, real data rather than padding. That is precisely the difference from the WHEN OTHER arms, where MOVE WS-FILE-ERROR-MESSAGE TO WS-RETURN-MSG moves the 80 bytes of the group declared at :86-105 - FILLER X(12) 'File Error: ' plus ERROR-OPNAME X(8) plus FILLER X(4) ' on ' plus ERROR-FILE X(9) plus FILLER X(15) ' returned RESP ' plus ERROR-RESP X(10) plus FILLER X(7) ',RESP2 ' plus ERROR-RESP2 X(10) plus FILLER X(5), which re-sums as 12+8+4+9+15+10+7+10+5 = 80 - into the same PIC X(75) and loses exactly the closing five-space FILLER, so nothing but padding goes. :532 then moves the surviving 75 bytes into ERRMSGO PIC X(78), re-padding by exactly 3, which is why the expected image measures 78 and ends in three spaces where the dropped digits stood. The two response codes are not case data and cannot drift: CustomerRepository reports the batch status FileStatus.NOT_FOUND 23, AccountViewController.cicsResp translates it to FileStatus.NOTFND = 13 and the reason code to FileStatus.NO_REASON_CODE = 0, and responseCodeImage renders each PIC S9(09) COMP value as nine unsigned digits left justified in PIC X(10) with one pad space - 000000013 and 000000000 - every one of them a compile-time constant, so the composed text is identical on every run (practice B7). The rest follows from the two flags. 1200 takes its ELSE at :464 because EIBCALEN is 172, and with FLG-ACCTFILTER-BLANK false :468 echoes the typed CC-ACCT-ID into ACCTSIDO. FOUND-ACCT-IN-MASTER satisfies the OR at :471-472, so the ten account items at :473-490 are projected from ACCTDAT row 49: ACSTTUSO Y; the three PIC X(10) dates 2011-04-22, 2023-03-09 and 2023-03-09 from ACCT-OPEN-DATE, from ACCT-EXPIRAION-DATE carrying CVACT01Y own misspelling, and from ACCT-REISSUE-DATE; ACCT-GROUP-ID as ten spaces; and the five PIC S9(10)V99 amounts through PIC +ZZZ,ZZZ,ZZZ.99 at width 15 - +        492.00 from the stored image 00000004920{ whose trailing overpunch is a digit and a sign in one byte, +      6,169.00, +      4,587.00, and +           .00 for both cycle amounts. FOUND-CUST-IN-MASTER is never set, so the IF at :493 is skipped and all eighteen customer items stay LOW-VALUES - x'00', not spaces and not an edited zero - which is the proof that the customer read failed rather than returned a blank record. INFOMSGC is DFHNEUTR rather than the DFHBMDAR of :568 because :528-530 flipped WS-NO-INFO-MESSAGE, set at :689, to WS-PROMPT-FOR-INPUT before :567 tested it, which is also why INFOMSGO carries the prompt of :113-114 - a literal of exactly 40 characters, counted, which fills WS-INFO-MSG PIC X(40) with no padding of its own and then gains five trailing spaces on the way into INFOMSGO PIC X(45). INPUT-ERROR is set at :840, yet it changes nothing about the exit: 9000-READ-ACCT runs inside the ELSE at :368, after the IF INPUT-ERROR at :364 was already evaluated, so the arm still performs 1000-SEND-MAP at :371-372 and leaves by the GO TO COMMON-RETURN at :373, bypassing the trailing IF INPUT-ERROR at :387-392 and reaching :395 - a forward-only GO TO reproduced as a plain return with its evaluation order and fall-through outcome intact (rule R7). 1400 moves LIT-THISMAPSET and LIT-THISMAP at :579-580 and SETs CDEMO-PGM-REENTER at :581, so the reply names COACTVW, CACTVWA and context 1, and the whole conversation - AID, commarea and screen values - travels in the payload with no server-side session state (gate G37, rule R6). CDEMO-CUST-ID and CDEMO-CARD-NUM are populated here, unlike in the cross-reference failure cases, because the NORMAL arm at :739-740 ran first. COACTVWC writes nothing - its only file verbs are the three EXEC CICS READs at :727, :776 and :826 - so expectedWrites is empty, all five seeded rows are pinned unchanged on the final-state channel, and expectedReturnCode is 0: an online NOTFND builds a message and paints a screen, and COACTVWC contains no CALL 'CEE3ABD', so neither an abend nor a non-zero status is asserted anywhere. Provenance: every expected value here is statically derived from app/cbl/COACTVWC.cbl, from the 300-byte CVACT01Y, 50-byte CVACT03Y and 500-byte CVCUS01Y layouts including their FILLER spans, from the xxxI PICTURE clauses of app/cpy-bms/COACTVW.CPY and from the real app/data/ASCII fixtures - and none of it was captured from a live COBOL execution, which this environment cannot run (risk R-A). The images are US-ASCII, the clock is pinned at 2022-07-19T23:15:58 so CURDATEO is 07/19/22 and CURTIMEO is 23:15:58, TITLE01O comes from app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy:19 and TITLE02O from its ACTIVE :22 with :21 commented out, and the cross-reference rows are seeded at the fixture own 36 bytes and padded to the 50 CVACT03Y declares by the declared normalisation (gate G16, risk R-F).
